title: Correct cross-window token attribution when streaming frames interleave and rate limiter enforces partial drops
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: The metering pipeline misattributes or drops input/output token credits when streaming frames from a single session are interleaved with other concurrent streams and the rate limiter triggers partial drops or backpressure. This leads to customers either being under-billed (missing output crediting) or over-billed (duplicate attribution) depending on timing and retry semantics.

Background: Our streaming stack splits streaming responses into frames and marks them with stream offsets. The metering aggregator materializes token counts per frame into time-windowed buckets for quota enforcement and billing. When the rate limiter throttles and causes partial frame buffering, cancellation, or server-side drops, the aggregator sometimes fails to: (1) detect final frame boundaries, (2) deduplicate retransmitted fragments, or (3) assign fragments to the correct logical session/window. The result: inconsistent final token totals for sessions that hit rate limits or experience mid-stream model switch/fallback.

Why it's urgent: This affects billing correctness for customers under high-throughput or bursty workloads and can cause quota mis-enforcement (false positives) that block legitimate traffic. We've observed this in internal dashboards and at least one customer support ticket reporting unexplained quota consumption during a traffic spike.
observed_behavior: During a controlled replay of interleaved streams with induced rate-limiter drop at t=+2s, aggregated token totals differed from ground truth by +/- 1-3 tokens per stream in 27% of traces and by up to 120 tokens in one long-running session that experienced repeated backpressure and retransmits.
expected_behavior: All stream frames from a session should be accounted exactly once and attributed to the correct session/window. When parts are dropped by rate limiter and not retried, those drops must be excluded from billed totals, and when retried/re-sent, deduplication should prevent double-counting. Final session totals must be stable and deterministically derived from stream terminal events (end_of_stream / final_frame marker), not transient buffering artifacts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start two concurrent streaming sessions A and B to the same model with interleaved output (A emits frame, B emits, A emits, ...).
2) Configure rate-limiter to allow base throughput but reject/buffer 1 out of every 5 frames (simulate partial drops/backpressure).
3) Simulate a client reconnect that resends last N frames after a short pause (to emulate retry semantics).
4) Observe metering aggregator logs and compare per-session token totals to network-level packet capture (ground truth).
5) Repeat with model fallback mid-stream (server switches to a lower-capacity variant) and with different batch window sizes (50ms, 200ms).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Maya: Reproduced locally using replay harness. Root cause narrows to window assignment logic in metering-aggregator when frames arrive out-of-order relative to end_of_stream marker.

2026-03-11 - Ethan: Confirmed dedupe key generation currently uses (session_id, frame_seq) but retries sometimes change frame_seq on client-side resends; need stronger idempotency key (session_id, frame_hash, sequence_hint).

2026-03-11 - SRE (J. Morales): Rate limiter introduces artificial buffering that moves frames into a later aggregation window; aggregator assumes monotonic frame timestamps and doesn't re-evaluate window when final_frame flag arrives from a delayed path.

2026-03-12 - Data (L. Nguyen): Dashboard link shows spike in 'mismatch_count' correlated with rate-limiter throttles for region us-west-2 between 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-02. Estimated revenue variance: ~ $1.2K across accounts for that week.

2026-03-12 - Decision: Implement three-pronged fix: reliable idempotency keys, end_of_stream re-windowing logic, and a lightweight audit checkpoint that reconciles per-session totals before committing billing events.

resolution_plan: 1) Implement robust idempotency key: (session_id, frame_hash, client_sequence_hint). Use a cheap streaming hash (Murmur3) computed on tokenizer bytes to avoid dependency on client sequence numbers.

2) Modify aggregator to defer final bucket commit until it has seen an end_of_stream or a checkpoint timeout; when end_of_stream arrives, reassign any late frames that were slotted into adjacent windows based on final_frame timestamp.

3) Add audit checkpoint: before emitting billing events for a session, compute a reconcile fingerprint and persist to a short-lived audit log; if reconciliation mismatch occurs, escalate to retry path instead of committing invoiceable tokens.

4) Add unit and integration tests covering: retries with altered sequence numbers, rate-limiter-induced buffering, interleaved streams with mid-stream model switch, and high-concurrency stress with small aggregation windows.
5) Canary roll the patch to a single region with synthetic traffic; monitor mismatch_count and billing_event_latency for regressions.
6) Post-mortem & customer comms if we detect historical variance exceeding threshold (>$500/account-week).
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end test harness shows zero token mismatch across 10k randomized interleaved-stream traces with induced rate-limiter faults.
2) Production canary shows mismatch_count reduced to baseline (<= 0.1%) and no increase in billing_event_latency beyond 10% of pre-change SLO.
3) PR merged with perf benchmarks demonstrating hash overhead <0.5% CPU on p95 workloads and no increase in tail latency for aggregator commit path.
4) Post-deploy audit job verifies previous 7 days of billing events for canary region and flags any deltas; if deltas exist they are under $500 total for region.
5) Documentation updated: metering semantics doc (confluence ID: MTR-1122) revised to describe idempotency keys and re-windowing behavior.
6) No customer escalations related to quota/overbilling after full rollout for two weeks.
